transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-08-05
Start: 15:10 PDT
Duration: ~53 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Asha (Redwood Solutions), Liam (Zeta CTO), Priya (Zeta Head of Security), Carlos (Infra)

Summary: (auto) Focused on encryption ops — BYOK and HSM onboarding flow, auditability requirements and residency constraints. Action items captured at end.

00:00 Jordan: okay everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll give folks a minute to pop in, but the plan — Maya and I will run through our proposed BYOK/HSM flow for Redwood Private and then go into ops, rotation and audit questions
00:22 Priya: hi all, sorry running a little late, Priya here. main thing for us is we're under SOC 2 and ISO obligations and need to make sure the key lifecycle map meets audit expectations
00:34 Jordan: totally, that's exactly why we wanted to walk through the ops. Maya, you want to start with architecture?
00:38 Maya: yeah sure, so high level — for Private deployments we support envelope encryption; application data is encrypted by a data key, the data key is encrypted by a KMS customer master key. For BYOK we integrate with customer KMS endpoints or an H-S-M cluster via KMIP or cloud HSM APIs. sometimes I say K-M-S and mix terms, but the flow is: Redwood runtime requests a data key from the KMS, uses it for local encryption, then discards the plaintext. the ciphertext key is stored with the object metadata.
01:10 Carlos: quick question, does Redwood persist any plaintext keys or ever cache them long-term? we've seen some vendors retain keys in memory and that worries us
01:18 Maya: good question. short answer: no persistent plaintext storage. We may hold the plaintext data key in process memory for the duration of the request/segment to encrypt or decrypt, and we scrub memory. we also support a KV cache for tokens but not for secret key material — sorry I said K-V cache earlier, that's different.
01:34 Liam: how does rotation work? If we rotate the CMK in the H-S-M do you need to re-encrypt all objects or do you support key-wrapping/reencryption?
01:42 Maya: we support key versioning and envelope rewrap. when a CMK rotates you can keep old wrapped keys so reads can still decrypt; for a rewrap sweep we offer a background job that will re-encrypt data keys with the new CMK, we can throttle it to avoid latency spikes. there is also a recommended strategy where you keep the previous x versions for N days to allow a staged cutoff.
02:05 Priya: we need proof points for that — would you be able to provide a sample playbook of an automated rotation with a canary and rollback? that is, we want to see the exact steps a reviewer will see in the SOC 2 artifact.
02:18 Jordan: yes, Maya will put together the playbook. we'll include a canary example and the rollback path and timing.
02:23 Maya: also we can provide logs for key operations — each KMS call (GenerateDataKey, Encrypt, Decrypt, Rewrap) is logged with timestamp, principal, and request id. note: when using customer-managed HSM the audit trail is split between Redwood logs and the HSM vendor logs — we can correlate via request IDs.
02:45 Priya: correlation is important. our auditors want immutable audit logs. is the HSM log append-only? how do we guarantee tamper evidence?
02:53 Maya: depends on the HSM. if you use a FIPS 140-2 Level 3 HSM with hardware-backed logging we can store the HSM event export in a WORM storage bucket on your side, or we can stream copies into an SIEM. Redwood's control plane also keeps a separate audit stream with hash chaining — I should say that chaining is in our design doc, we'll share the link. sometimes the transcript auto-substitutes words, but you'll get the doc.
03:20 Nadia: two questions: first, for data residency, we need keys to be generated and stay within EU boundaries for EU-cust data. can Redwood restrict key usage by region and prevent cross-border key calls?
03:33 Maya: yes, our smart routing can pin requests by region. for Private you host the KMS endpoints in your VPC in the region you choose, so keys do not leave. for Hosted we'd use regionally isolated HSM clusters if you require it — but for strict residency we recommend Private + customer-managed KMS.
03:52 Carlos: what about performance — adding an external HSM per-Encrypt call could add latency on hot paths, how do you mitigate that?
04:00 Maya: we use envelope encryption to reduce HSM calls to only GenerateDataKey and Rewrap operations. normal token-by-token generation only touches the local data key. we also support short-lived cached data keys for a small window and strict TTL, and we can use batching for some workloads. we'll show latency numbers in the runbook.
04:22 Priya: okay. about BYOK — we prefer a dual-control model: one ops key holder and one security approver for key import. does Redwood support split approval or custodial separation during import?
04:34 Jordan: we do. for BYOK import we have an import protocol that can be gated behind RBAC + SAML groups; customers can require two-person approval before we accept and activate the CMK. the activation step can be locked behind SCIM groups and an approval webhook to your ticketing.
04:52 Liam: what about escrow — do you require us to hand keys to Redwood? we want the keys to be under our exclusive control, no escrow unless explicitly arranged for disaster recovery
05:03 Jordan: we don't require escrow. BYOK implies control remains with you. we can provide optional managed backup of wrapped keys encrypted under a recovery key you manage or a split escrow model if you want DR, but that's opt-in and documented in the contract.
05:22 Priya: auditors will ask about split knowledge and key custodianship; can you document who at Redwood has ability to call decrypt or decrypt through the control plane?
05:31 Maya: yes, we can export an access matrix. operationally, Redwood engineers do not have a master key to decrypt customer data. control plane operations are separated by roles, and decryption is only possible with access to the wrapped key and the KMS — in BYOK the KMS access is controlled by customer credentials. we'll include the RBAC mapping.
05:52 Carlos: how are secrets injected into Redwood Private? we're looking for an automated terraform/secret-manager onboarding pattern, not manual copy+pasting
06:01 Asha: we have Terraform modules and an onboarding ansible/terraform flow that creates the KMS integration endpoints and service principals. we can provide sample Terraform for GCP/AWS/Azure HSM and on-prem KMIP connectors. we'll attach the snippets.
06:15 Priya: do you support HSM like Thales or Utimaco or only cloud HSMs?
06:19 Maya: we support both. KMIP connector works for many appliance HSMs like Thales, Utimaco, and also cloud HSM APIs from AWS/Google/Azure. sometimes there are vendor-specific quirks, we test the integration during the onboarding dry-run.
06:34 Liam: audit question: can we get per-request telemetry associated to a business request id? our incident process ties data access to ticket ids
06:42 Maya: yes, we can pass a correlation id through the Redwood API and attach it to KMS calls; logs will include that ID so you can grep and reconcile in your SIEM.
06:53 Priya: about TLS and in-transit — what's the cipher suite and do you do mutual TLS to the HSM?
07:00 Jordan: for control plane and KMS endpoints we enforce TLS1.2+ (prefer TLS1.3) and support mTLS for customer-managed endpoints. the HSM connector uses mutual TLS or KMIP with secure channel depending on vendor.
07:18 Priya: good. another regulator check: what about key rotation policies stored as code? auditors like to see policy-as-code for rotation frequency and canaries
07:27 Maya: we recommend rotation intervals and can store rotation policies in our config repo as YAML and provide the repo snapshot as evidence. we'll provide a sample policy-as-code snippet.
07:40 Carlos: on the topic of re-encryption, is there a scheduled window where rewraps happen? we need to ensure rewrap doesn't impact SLAs for ingestion
07:49 Maya: by default we run a background rewrap job at low-priority, with concurrency limits. you can set a maintenance window. also there's a preview mode where rewrap operations are staged and metrics reported before committing.
08:05 Liam: curious about key compromise — if a CMK is suspected leaked, what's the recommended emergency process?
08:13 Maya: typical steps: revoke/disable the CMK in the HSM, create new CMK, start emergency rewrap for high-value objects first, revoke any service principals potentially affected, and rotate any tokens. we'll provide an incident runbook with timelines and roles.
08:30 Priya: will that be part of SOC 2 testing scenarios? our auditor expects tabletop exercises; want to include a compromise scenario and response time metrics.
08:39 Jordan: yes, we can help run a tabletop with you and provide the scripts for the auditor.
08:44 Carlos: on key import — do you support split import where the key material is split into shares and reassembled in the HSM?
08:52 Maya: for some HSMs we can use split knowledge and import tokens where key shares are combined in the appliance. it's vendor-dependent but supported in principle.
09:02 Priya: certification: does Redwood maintain SOC 2 Type II? we saw references on the site but want to confirm scope includes private connectors and key operation controls
09:12 Jordan: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II with the security and availability principles; we can share the SOC 2 package and map the controls to the key lifecycle. some on-prem connectors are covered differently and we'll annotate the scope.
09:25 Priya: also do you have an ISO 27001 cert?
09:29 Jordan: we are in the process of getting ISO 27001; current customers with strict requirements often pair Redwood with their own on-prem KMS to meet the residual risk profiles.
09:38 Priya: okay. about SSO/RBAC — we want fine-grained roles for key ops: key-importer, key-operator, key-approver, read-only-audit. can you align Redwood roles to our SAML groups?
09:50 Maya: yes we map roles to SAML attributes and SCIM provisioning. we also support temporary elevation via an approval flow for emergency ops, with timebox and audit trail.
10:05 Carlos: is there a way to run a dry-run where the HSM is used in 'simulate' mode so we can measure performance without promoting keys to production?
10:14 Maya: we support a test mode and a staging HSM connector. you can run the rewrap sweep and simulate load; we will label logs accordingly so it's clear what was test versus prod.
10:25 Priya: logging format — will you provide structured logs (JSON) with fields for timestamp, request_id, principal, operation, region, and correlation_id?
10:35 Maya: yes, structured JSON logs are available and we will provide sample schema.
10:40 Liam: can Redwood provide a non-repudiation proof? how do we prove that a particular key operation happened and who approved it?
10:49 Maya: the combination of HSM tamper logs, Redwood audit stream with hash chaining, and the approvals recorded via the SCIM/SAML mapping and ticketing webhook provide that evidence. we'll show an example timeline in the artifact.
11:05 Priya: about encryption algorithm — do you support AES-GCM only or other ciphers? auditors sometimes demand specific approved algorithms
11:12 Maya: we support AES-256-GCM for data keys; for KMIP/HSM we can negotiate algorithms per vendor, and we document algorithm policy per customer.
11:22 Carlos: anything about KMS quotas or throttling that we should know? we need predictable behavior under load
11:29 Maya: we'll surface rate limits and request throttling in the onboarding runbook; for Dedicated we can provision capacity and Autoscaler rules to meet throughput targets.
11:39 Priya: regarding retention of logs — auditors want 7 years for some financial data; can you store audit logs that long and provide search access?
11:48 Jordan: Redwood's observability retention tiers are configurable; we can retain high-fidelity audit logs for long tails via an add-on, and we can export them to your long-term storage.
11:58 Liam: question on export controls and cross-border key materials — our legal flagged that some keys cannot be exported outside of EU without export paperwork
12:07 Maya: we can restrict export and block key wrap/unwrapping from other regions by policy. we'll also add the approach to the compliance artifact.
12:16 Priya: what about periodic audits — will we get an attestation about how keys were handled in the last 12 months?
12:24 Jordan: yes, we can provide an annual key handling attestation and ad-hoc reports for specific periods.
12:33 Carlos: any automated tests you run to ensure keys aren't accidentally leaked in logs or traces?
12:38 Maya: we have automated scans for PII and secret patterns in logs, and an internal SRE gate that prevents commit of plaintext secrets; we'll provide details in the security controls doc.
12:50 Priya: let's discuss the onboarding timeline — what does a typical HSM onboarding schedule look like?
12:56 Maya: typical is 4–6 weeks: week 1 discovery and matrix, week 2 test connector and sample imports, week 3 dry-run rewrap and performance testing, week 4 go-live and audit evidence handoff. more complex networks or on-prem air-gapped setups add time.
13:15 Liam: do you run penetration tests specifically on the key handling modules?
13:20 Jordan: Redwood engages third-party pentest firms and we can run scoping tests around key handling on an agreed schedule; results are available under NDA.
13:29 Priya: on RBAC audit trail — do you provide a ledger of who approved key import and when?
13:36 Maya: approval events are logged and we can export them as CSV/JSON with an approval artifact id tying to the ticketing system.
13:44 Carlos: curious about metrics — can you give us latency percentiles for GenerateDataKey and Decrypt under normal load?
13:52 Maya: we'll include benchmark numbers; typical GenerateDataKey via cloud HSM is 5–20ms, network dependent; Decrypt varies by payload, we'll share P50/P95 numbers from our test harness.
14:05 Priya: one more on legal — will Redwood sign a KMP (key management policy) addendum or KMA?
14:12 Jordan: we can execute a KMA addendum that records key ownership, responsibilities, and SLAs for key ops. we'll involve legal.
14:20 Liam: ok let's talk about the test window — we're aiming for week of Aug 18 as a dry-run, need 2 hours of scheduled HSM access for the vendor and a maintenance ticket
14:30 Jordan: noted, we'll propose times in the next email.

--- closing and recap ---
51:10 Jordan: quick recap: Redwood to share BYOK/HSM runbook, Terraform snippets, rotation playbook, and SOC2 mapping. Zeta will confirm regions and schedule the Aug 18 dry-run. action items listed in the doc.
51:30 Priya: thanks all, will look for the runbook and confirm scheduling.
51:38 Liam: thanks, appreciate the detail.
51:42 Jordan: great, we'll follow up with artifacts and a calendar invite for the dry-run.
51:48 Maya: thanks everyone.

Artifacts mentioned: link: https://redwood.ai/docs/byok-runbook (sample), link: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2-package (sample), onboarding Terraform snippets (attached in follow-up)
